sentiment.instructions: Decide whether the tweet carries an explicit positive or negative stance, through feeling words, emoticons, eager hype, praise or disparagement, or a clearly good or bad event. If there is no such signal, choose neutral, even if the author talks about themselves. Exclamation marks alone are not a signal.

criteria.positive: Positive feeling or praise: love, like, fun, best, perfect, brilliant, impressed, amazing, cool, hope, pray, blessings, celebrate, can't wait, let's go, wow, :). Includes hedged praise of the author's own experience ('may be the best I've seen'), confident praise or defense of someone, and the author's eager anticipation of their own concert, show or outing. Also eager promotions (check it out, come support, please share, get your tickets now, win), condolences that bless someone, and completed successes such as titles, finals reached, records or historic firsts.
criteria.neutral: No stance signal. Covers flat plans, event notices (meeting, RSVP, register, info session, airtime), ticket sales, spam, requests even with a passing thanks or <3, news headlines, scores and in-progress game updates, trivia, neutral questions and speculation. Also hedged comparisons about politicians or celebrities ('more real than'), jokes, comic hyperbole about oneself (I'm dead, lol, lmao, not ready), light wry sports commentary, and headlines whose negative words describe no real harm.
criteria.negative: Negative feeling: sad, hate, annoyed, ugh, ACK, wtf, damn, bad mood, can't sleep, going to die, miss, sucks, disappointed, :(. Also disparagement without feeling words: belittling comparisons, mocking remarks about someone, sarcastic labels, cynical rhetorical questions about politicians or institutions, and complaints ('why haven't they…'). Includes insults, hostile political or religious arguments, and real harm: deaths, attacks, riots, bombings, crimes, charges, scandals, injuries, deficits, product failures.
